content.title: Kennedy Space Center | Location, Address & Directions
content.text: Your Definitive Guide on How to Get to the Kennedy Space CenterKennedy Space CenterDirectionsWhere is the Kennedy Space Center?Address: Space Commerce Way, Merritt Island, FL 32953, USA | Find on Maps The Kennedy Space Center (KSC) is located on Merritt Island. It is situated on the east coast of Florida, near the town of Titusville. The center is approximately 34 miles (55 kilometers) east of Orlando. Closest landmark: Blue Origin Rocket Factory (1 mile away)Getting to KSCPlease note that there is no direct public transportation available to Kennedy Space Center. Driving to the location is the best option. The entrance to Kennedy Space Center is located on Space Commerce Way and the Visitor Complex is approximately 1.2 miles from this point.Getting There by CarFrom Coco BeachHead north on A1A to State Road (SR) 528 west, and take exit #49 for SR 3 toward Merritt Island/Kennedy Space Center. Make a right onto SR 3, continue north for around 8 miles, turn left onto Space Commerce Way. Travel 1.5 miles and you'll find the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex on the right.From OrlandoGo east on SR 50 for about 50 miles and turn right at the intersection onto SR 405 after you pass I-95. Follow signs for approximately 10 miles and turn right onto Space Commerce Way. Continue for approximately 1.2 miles and the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex will come on your left.From Daytona BeachHead south on I-95 and take Exit #215 onto Highway 50, then make a left turn. Proceed to turn right onto SR 405, following the signs for about 10 miles. Afterward, take a right onto Space Commerce Way and travel approximately 1.2 miles to find the entrance to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex on the left.From MiamiTake I-95 North and exit at #212, turning right onto SR 407. Follow SR 407 until it ends at SR 405, then turn right. Stay on SR 405, following the signs for Kennedy Space Center for about 7.5 miles. Subsequently, turn right onto Space Commerce Way and travel approximately 1.2 miles to find the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex on your left.Kennedy Space Center Parking FacilitiesParking at the Visitor Complex: The Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex has a parking lot of its own to accommodate automobiles, motorcycles, and bigger vehicles like RVs. The parking fee is collected at the entrance, right upon entry to the area.Parking Fees:Motorcycles: $5Automobiles: $15Oversized vehicles, motor homes, and RVs: $20Parking Hours: 9am to 5pm and 24 hours on weekends. Parking is accessible 30 minutes before the Visitor Complex opens.Where else is parking available at the Kennedy Space Center?There is no other parking space around the Kennedy Space Center. It is best and safest to park inside the premises.Getting There by BusThere is no direct public transport to get to the Kennedy Space Center. However, you can take bus numbers 11, 111, and 436S from Orlando and alight at Grey Hound station or any of the bus stops at Titusville. From here, you must take a taxi to get to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.For hassle-free travel, opt for Kennedy Space Center tickets with round-trip transportation:Kennedy Space Center Tickets with Round-Trip TransportationTickets to Kennedy Space Center with Explore TourSmall Group VIP Tour of Kennedy Space CenterKennedy Space Center bus toursVisitor Tips for Getting to KSCThe best way to get to the Kennedy Space Center is to drive there since there is no direct public transportation available.The nearest airpor is Melbourne (MLB) Airport which is a 51-minute drive from the Visitor Complex.If you are driving, please note that there is a new entrance located on the Space Commerce Way and that you must follow all posted speed limits since the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex is located on federal property. Any traffic violations will result in heavy fines. Alternatively, you can also opt for a shuttle bus with round-trip transportation. Keep in mind that there is no direct public transportation available directly to the Visitor Complex.Is there public transportation to get to the KSC?No, there is no direct public transportation to get to the Kennedy Space Center. Your best bet is to drive down or opt for a ticket with round-trip transportation.Are there any landmarks nearby?The closest landmark to the Kennedy Space Center is the Blue Origin Rocket Factory, located just 1 mile away down Space Commerce Way. This facility is part of the growing space industry in the area, contributing to advancements in rocket technology and space exploration.Which is the nearest airport?The nearest airport to the Kennedy Space Center is Melbourne International Airport (MLB), located approximately 29.7 miles away. Another major option is Orlando International Airport (MCO).How far is the KSC from Orlando International Airport?The Kennedy Space Center is approximately 50 miles east of Orlando International Airport. The drive typically takes about 47 to 49 minutes.Are there any toll roads on the way to the Kennedy Space Center?Yes, there are toll roads on the way to the Kennedy Space Center. The most common route is via the Beachline Expressway (SR 528) typically incurs tolls of around $6 each way. Be prepared with cash or a toll pass.Which is the fastest way to get to the Kennedy Space Center?The fastest way to get to the Kennedy Space Center is by car. It is about 10 miles from Coco Beach, about 60 miles from Orlando, and about 12 miles from Daytona Beach.Which is the cheapest way to get to KSC?The cheapest way to get to the Kennedy Space Center is to drive down by car.
